title: Hazel and the Mixtape
premise: Hazel Vasquez, the overlooked statistician for the Marlowe High basketball team, has spent senior year keeping score from the bench and counting down to graduation. When his late grandmother's recipe box yields coded instructions instead of recipes, Hazel learns she was part of a network that protected the town's undocumented families — and that the final safe deposit key is hidden somewhere in the school, which the district plans to demolish after championship season. As the team's star is benched by a falsified eligibility scandal Hazel's own records can expose, he must choose between protecting his stats-verified truth and the loyalty of the friends who kept him invisible. In the end, Hazel wins the championship by refusing to play the rigged game, recovers his grandmother's legacy with hours to spare, and finally takes up visible space — as the boy who kept the real score.
about_author: Mara Thackeray is a former high school math teacher from the Central Valley who spent a decade keeping scoreboards and listening to teenagers in empty gyms. She writes stories about quiet kids who discover the world was always bigger than the box score.

chapters.title: The Bench Is a Kind of Math
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Opening game of senior season: Hazel charts stats from the scorer's table, invisible by design, while his best friend Deon carries the team. He narrates the countdown to graduation — 187 days. Emotional beat: comfortable numbness, with a hairline crack of wanting more.

chapters.title: Cardamom and Ciphers
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Clearing out his grandmother's kitchen, Hazel finds her recipe box: among the abuelita recipes are index cards of numbers, names, and a map of the high school drawn in her handwriting. The last card reads 'For when they come for us. Finish it, mijo.' Emotional beat: grief curdling into unease.

chapters.title: 187 Days
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel tries to treat the cards like a school puzzle while life continues: practice, a growing rapport with team captain Priya, and the district's announcement that Marlowe High will be demolished in June. Emotional beat: denial dressed up as productivity.

chapters.title: What Grandma Kept
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel's mother reveals fragments: grandma Rosa housed families in the eighties, kept records, and trusted no institutions. The cards are a ledger — proof, addresses, a key to a safe deposit box Hazel can't locate. Emotional beat: the weight of inherited secrecy.

chapters.title: The Rigged Bracket
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya notices the seeding committee has slotted Marlowe against an undefeated rival with a star player whose eligibility paperwork is suspiciously clean. She asks Hazel to dig into the numbers. Emotional beat: indignation finding an ally.

chapters.title: Anomalies
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel's statistical audit uncovers grade changes and residency fraud benefiting the rival star — and evidence someone inside Marlowe's own administration helped bury a similar case years ago. The handwriting on one old memo feels familiar. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt turning to dread.

chapters.title: Deon's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Deon's POV. Deon, whose scholarship depends on a deep playoff run, begs Hazel to sit on the findings until after the season. Loyalty vs. truth takes human form in a locker-room argument. Emotional beat: friendship under load, bending but not breaking.

chapters.title: The Card That Isn't a Recipe
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Decoding the index cards, Hazel realizes the 'ingredients' are landmarks in the school — the gym rafters, the library's old card catalog, a tile in the east stairwell. Grandma Rosa's trail runs through the building slated for demolition. Emotional beat: wonder, and a ticking clock made physical.

chapters.title: After Hours in the Card Catalog
chapters.summary: Hazel and Priya's POV, alternating. A midnight break-in to the library yields a hollow drawer and a brass key stamped with a bank name that closed in 1999. They're nearly caught by a night custodian who recognizes the key — and Rosa. Emotional beat: conspiratorial intimacy; the first time Hazel feels seen.

chapters.title: The Custodian's Testimony
chapters.summary: Custodian Ernesto's POV. Ernesto tells them Rosa's network used the school as a waystation; he was one of the children she hid. The 'key' is a promise: whoever holds it owes protection to whoever comes asking. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as obligation, not treasure.

chapters.title: Eligibility
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The rival school's athletic director, tipped off, accuses Deon of the very fraud Hazel uncovered — a mirror-image smear using falsified transcripts. Deon is suspended from the team pending investigation. Emotional beat: injustice weaponized; rage with nowhere safe to go.

chapters.title: What the Numbers Say
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel can prove Deon's innocence and expose the rival star with the same dataset — but releasing it mid-season torpedoes the championship and drags his mother's family history into the light. He drafts the report and doesn't send it. Emotional beat: cowardice examined without excuse.

chapters.title: The Demolition Notice
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The district moves the demolition date up to the week after finals — before the bank's successor institution can process any claim. Hazel realizes the conspiracy he found in the sports paperwork and the one that buried Rosa's network may share a name: school board member Alvarado. Emotional beat: two mysteries snapping into one.

chapters.title: Alvarado's Ledger
chapters.summary: Priya and Hazel's POV. Digging through archived board minutes, they find Alvarado was the administrator who 'resolved' the old eligibility scandal — by destroying Rosa's records. The recipe box isn't just a legacy; it's the only surviving copy of the proof. Emotional beat: the past reaching into the present, hand outstretched.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Alvarado corners Hazel: stay quiet, and Deon is reinstated, the championship proceeds, everyone's future is safe. He frames it as mercy. Hazel, holding the report he never sent, understands exactly what kind of deal this is. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: 187 Becomes 12
chapters.summary: Deon's POV. Deon learns Hazel sat on the evidence to protect the team's run — and can't decide if that's loyalty or betrayal. A fractured conversation in Hazel's grandmother's empty kitchen. Emotional beat: the cost of silence made explicit; the friendship at its lowest point.

chapters.title: The Tile in the East Stairwell
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. With demolition crews already fencing the building, Hazel follows the final card to a loose tile and finds Rosa's sealed envelope: the account number, the names of every family she sheltered, and a letter telling Hazel he was always allowed to be seen. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into inheritance; tears in a stairwell.

chapters.title: The Report
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel submits everything — the eligibility fraud, Alvarado's old cover-up, the demolition's convenient timing — to the state athletic board and a local reporter, knowing it may end the season and his own standing. Deon, reading it before it goes out, adds a statement of his own. Emotional beat: the choice finally made; terror and relief in the same breath.

chapters.title: Forfeiture
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The board vacates the rival's wins; the championship is thrown into chaos; Alvarado resigns under investigation. The team must decide whether to play a rescheduled final that 'doesn't count' for the rival's star. They vote to play. Emotional beat: solidarity forged in wreckage.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel takes the floor for the first time all season when the team runs out of healthy bodies — and the boy who kept score finally plays, calling his own numbers. They win by two on a possession Hazel diagrammed. Emotional beat: visibility earned; joy without irony.

chapters.title: The Box on the Table
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. At Rosa's reopened safe deposit box, Hazel and the families from her ledger — Ernesto among them — claim the records and donate them to the county historical society, out of hiding forever. Hazel's mother reads her mother's letter aloud. Emotional beat: inheritance completed; belonging chosen.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. 187 days later: Hazel crosses the stage with his name pronounced correctly for once, the recipe box — now half recipes, half archive — under his arm. Deon's scholarship is restored; Priya is headed to coach; the school's demolition is paused pending landmark review. Hazel starts a new card for the box. Emotional beat: the sentence served, the count ended, the future open.
